title: Courses
subtitle: Upload a course you are going to ride and get a segment table and a pacing plan.
stillAir: Every speed and split assumes still air and dry pavement. A headwind will move them, and a group will beat these numbers on the flat.

target.label: Target
target.noneHelp: No target: a steady effort you could sustain for the whole course.
target.timeHelp: As h:mm:ss or h:mm. The plan works backwards from the finish, spending on the climbs where a watt buys the most time.
target.powerHelp: Watts, held as the average for the whole ride — above it on the climbs, below it on the descents. The finish time is whatever that produces.
target.badTimeDesc: Write the target as h:mm:ss or h:mm — for example 4:30:00.
target.badPowerDesc: Write the target in watts — a whole number above zero, for example 210.

list.deleteBody: "{name}", its analysis and the file you uploaded will be removed. This cannot be undone.

upload.drop: Drop a GPX course here, or click to choose one
upload.firstRunTitle: Plan a course before you ride it
upload.firstRunBody: Drop in the GPX of an event or a route you are about to ride. openkoutsi splits it into segments, works out what power to hold and how long each one takes at your own FTP and weight, and can write you a pacing plan.
upload.invalidFile: That is not a GPX file
upload.invalidFileDesc: A course is a route, so openkoutsi needs a .gpx file.
upload.name: Name
upload.namePlaceholder: Taken from the file if you leave this empty
upload.needBikeBody: The pacing physics needs to know your tyre width and riding position, so add a bike before uploading a course.

reason.no_elevation_data: This file has no elevation data, so gradients cannot be worked out from it.
reason.course_too_short: This course is too short to analyse.
reason.missing_rider_data: Set your FTP and weight on your profile first — the pacing physics needs both.

bikes.title: Your bikes
bikes.why: The pacing model reads two things off a bike: tyre width, which sets rolling resistance, and riding position, which sets how much air you push. Add and edit bikes in the garage.
bikes.empty: No bikes yet — add one in the garage.

segments.inferredLegend: Marked “inferred” means openkoutsi could not confirm a surface tag for that stretch — the class comes from the road type instead. It is a guess, not a reading.

refusal.title: That target time is not reachable
refusal.target_faster_than_physics: No human power gets round this course in the time you asked for. The fastest ride the model can produce is {fastest}.
refusal.exceeds_sustainable_power: Reaching that time would take an average of {required} × your FTP, which is more than anyone holds for a ride this long. The plan below is built around what you could actually sustain.
refusal.powerTitle: That is more power than you could hold
refusal.power_exceeds_sustainable: Holding {required} × your FTP for {duration} is more than anyone sustains. The splits below are exactly the ride you asked for — treat them as what it would take, not as a plan, and ease the target if you want one you can finish.

plan.title: Pacing plan
plan.getPlanHelp: Koutsi is given the segment table above — never the route itself — and writes how to ride it.
plan.thinking: Let me look at this course…
plan.error: Something went wrong writing your plan. Give it another go.

surface.addHelp: Match this course against OpenStreetMap to classify the road under it.
surface.unconfirmed: {distance} of that is unconfirmed — openkoutsi could not find a surface tag for it, so the class comes from the road type.
surface.asphaltNote: Asphalt is never confirmed: a road nobody has tagged looks exactly like smooth tarmac to openkoutsi, so those stretches could be either.

stillAirMatched: Every speed and split assumes still air. A headwind will move them, and it can move them a lot. Surfaces come from OpenStreetMap, and the ones marked inferred are a guess.
